meta.description: The 944th Operations Group administrative work center encompasses climate-controlled office suites, conference facilities, and computer workstations dedicated to flight records management, operational planning, and administrative duties.
meta.references:
Air Force Publications (Core Governing Directives):
DAFMAN 91-203, Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire, and Health Standards — Primary standard for office environments (specifically Chapter 10, Office Safety; Chapter 14, Material Handling/Lifting; Chapter 17, Electrical Safety).

DAFI 91-202, The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program — Mandates JSTO creation, safety indoctrination, and supervisor training documentation.

DAFMAN 91-204, Safety Investigations and Hazard Reporting — Outlines the mishap reporting pipeline and safety investigation procedures.

AFMAN 48-146, Occupational & Environmental Health Program — Governs Bioenvironmental Engineering assessments and workplace ergonomics.

Department of Defense & Federal Standards:
DoDI 6055.01, DoD Safety and Occupational Health (SOH) Program.

29 CFR 1910, OSHA General Industry Standards (specifically Subpart D for Walking-Working Surfaces, Subpart E for Means of Egress, Subpart S for Electrical, and 1910.1200 for Hazard Communication).

Local & Wing Policies (944 FW / Host Installation):
944 FW Mishap Prevention Program / Safety Supplement.

Building Emergency Action Plan (EAP) & Facility Evacuation Annex.

Base Fire Prevention Policy (governing portable space heaters, breakroom appliances, and egress clearances).

Prescribed Forms & Systems:
AF Form 55, Employee Safety and Health Record (or current digital Safety Management System/AFSAS equivalent).

AF Form 457, USAF Hazard Report.

AF Form 978, Supervisor's Report of Employee Injury/Illness.
meta.jhaNotes: Operational hazards in this environment primarily involve musculoskeletal fatigue and cumulative trauma disorders from prolonged visual display terminal (VDT) use and improper ergonomics; slips, trips, and falls caused by wet flooring, transition thresholds, or trailing cables; acute lower-back strain from manual material handling of copy paper cartons () and archive records; mechanical and tip-over risks associated with lateral filing cabinets, step stools, and motorized paper shredders; and electrical shock or fire hazards resulting from daisy-chained power strips, unapproved portable space heaters, or unattended breakroom appliances.

meta.medicalFacility:
Immediate Life-Threatening Emergencies:
Call Base Emergency Dispatch (911 DSN / (623) 856-5911 cell) or request Luke AFB dispatch.

Administer CPR/AED immediately if trained; assign a designated runner to the building exterior to guide arriving emergency responders.

Direct ambulance transport to the nearest designated trauma/emergency facility (e.g., Abrazo West Campus Level 1 Trauma Center, Banner Estrella).

Duty Status-Specific Treatment Channels:
Military Personnel (Active Duty / AGR / Title 10 Orders): Report to the 56th Medical Group Clinic (Luke AFB Clinic), Bldg 1022. For after-hours care, consult the TRICARE Nurse Advice Line (1-800-TRICARE) prior to seeking civilian urgent care.

Traditional Reservists (TRs / IDT Drill Status): Report to the 56 MDG or base urgent care during drill status. Immediate initiation of a Line of Duty (LOD) determination before the end of the drill period is mandatory.

DoD Civilians & Air Reserve Technicians (ARTs - Civilian Status): Initial emergency stabilization at the base clinic, followed by referral to designated Federal Employees' Compensation Act (FECA) / Office of Workers' Compensation Programs (OWCP) medical providers. Issue Form CA-16 (Authorization for Examination/Treatment) and file Form CA-1 (Notice of Traumatic Injury).

Work Center First Aid Kit Guidelines:
Kit location, designated custodian, and monthly replenishment checks.

Strict adherence to Air Force policy prohibiting oral medications (e.g., aspirin, ibuprofen) in unit first aid kits to prevent allergic reactions.

Mishap Documentation & Reporting:
Completion and submission of AF Form 978 (Supervisor's Report of Employee Injury/Illness) within 24 hours to the 944 FW Safety Office for entry into the Air Force Safety Automated System (AFSAS).
meta.evacuationRoute:
Entrances and exits are located on all four sides of the facility (North, South, East, and West). Personnel must evacuate via the nearest clear, unobstructed exit away from smoke or hazards.

Primary Muster Point: SOUTH PARKING LOT. All personnel must report immediately to their section supervisor / muster coordinator for 100% accountability.
meta.shelterInPlace: Primary SIP Location: ROOM 130 (MAIN BRIEFING ROOM). Designated secure collective sheltering location during hazardous material releases, airborne environmental threats, base chemical/biological alerts, or severe weather events. Ensure doors are closed, HVAC is set appropriately per EAP instructions, and accountability is verified.
meta.activeShooterMethods: Executed strictly IAW Luke AFB Procedures:• RUN (Evacuate): If a safe path is accessible, evacuate immediately via the nearest exit (utilizing any of the four building exits). Leave belongings behind. Keep hands visible with fingers spread.• HIDE (Lockdown / Shelter): If evacuation is unsafe, seek immediate cover. Secure and barricade doors (utilizing Room 130 or inner office suites), turn off lights, close window blinds, silence mobile phones/radios, and remain silent out of sight.• FIGHT (Defend): As an absolute last resort and only when life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt or incapacitate the shooter using aggressive improvised measures and team commitment.• Law Enforcement Arrival (56 SFS): When Security Forces arrive, remain calm, keep hands raised and empty, do not make sudden moves or point, and immediately obey all verbal instructions.• Alerts & Reporting: Monitor AtHoc emergency mass notifications; notify 56 SFS BDOC ((623) 856-6322) or Base Emergency Dispatch ((623) 856-5911) as soon as safe.
meta.adverseWeatherShelter: Relocate to interior windowless spaces—including Room 130 or central interior hallways—during severe Arizona dust storms (haboobs) and convective squalls.
